## Answer

**The DPLM-2 paper does not cover family/GO/EC/text/function-keyword conditioning at all.** Its entire notion of "conditional generation" is structural/mechanical — conditioning on sequence, on structure, or on a partial mixed-modal motif. Nothing in your [plans/conditional_dplm_pfam.md](plans/conditional_dplm_pfam.md) direction (Pfam ID, EC, GO, function text) comes from this paper.

### What "conditional" means in the paper

The paper frames every protein task as conditioning *between the two modalities it models*: amino-acid sequence $\mathbf{s}$ and backbone structure $\mathbf{x}$ ([dplm2_paper.md:186-205](dplm2_paper.md#L186-L205)). Concretely, Tab. `[tab:task]` lists five tasks, all defined by which modality is input vs output:

| Task | Conditioning | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Forward folding | sequence → structure | §4.2 ([L609](dplm2_paper.md#L609)) |
| Inverse folding | structure → sequence | §4.3 ([L639](dplm2_paper.md#L639)) |
| Unconditional co-generation | neither | §4.1 ([L440](dplm2_paper.md#L440)) |
| Motif scaffolding | mixed-modal motif (partial seq + partial struct) | §4.4 ([L663](dplm2_paper.md#L663)) |

The contributions paragraph at [L118-130](dplm2_paper.md#L118-L130) is the only place "conditional generation tasks" is enumerated, and it lists exactly those four: folding, inverse folding, motif scaffolding. At [L203-205](dplm2_paper.md#L203-L205) it generalizes: "single or mixed-modal conditioning for partial generation, *e.g.*, motif-scaffolding and antibody design."

### Motif scaffolding (the closest thing to "function-conditioned" design)

§4.4 ([L663-702](dplm2_paper.md#L663-L702)) and Appendix ([L881-929](dplm2_paper.md#L881-L929)) describe the 24-problem Yim et al. benchmark. "Function" here means *a fixed functional motif* — the user supplies the motif's 3D coordinates and sequence, the model scaffolds around it. Success = `scTM > 0.8` and `motif-RMSD < 1 Å` against the native motif ([L677-681](dplm2_paper.md#L677-L681)). There is **no** family ID, EC number, GO term, InterPro domain, natural-language description, or retrieval mechanism anywhere in this protocol.

### Explicit absences (verified by grep)

The paper contains **zero** occurrences of: Pfam, InterPro, GO, EC number, enzyme commission, gene ontology, keyword, taxonomy, natural-language prompt, or protein-text conditioning. The only matches for "function"/"description" are:
- generic prose about sequence→function ("structure governs function", [L6](dplm2_paper.md#L6))
- motif-scaffolding's notion of "preserve motif's structure hence the functions" ([L696](dplm2_paper.md#L696))
- "designing protein structures for specific functions, such as enzymes" in the *related work* on RFDiffusion ([L970-972](dplm2_paper.md#L970-L972))
- "SwissProt" used purely as a training-data source name ([L156](dplm2_paper.md#L156), [L295](dplm2_paper.md#L295), [L589](dplm2_paper.md#L589), [L731](dplm2_paper.md#L731), [L808](dplm2_paper.md#L808), [L813](dplm2_paper.md#L813)) — never as a conditioning annotation source.

### Implication for your roadmap

This is consistent with what your own [missing-code.md](plans/missing-code.md) found: the paper reports "DPLM-2 any-to-any conditional generation / motif scaffolding — *Partially*" with "no motif-specific finetuning config." The family/GO/EC/text direction in your plans is genuinely **new work**, not paper reproduction. If you want a literature precedent for the function/annotation-conditioning angle, your [prodva_pdfbench_notes.md](plans/prodva_pdfbench_notes.md) (ProDVA) and [procalm_report.md](plans/procalm_report.md) (ProCALM's EC/taxonomy adapters) are the right references — not the DPLM-2 paper.

## Summary

**CFP-Gen is built directly on top of DPLM-650M and turns it into a multimodal-conditioned sequence diffusion model.** This is the closest published precedent to the post-Pfam function-conditioning phase of your [plans/conditional_dplm_pfam.md](plans/conditional_dplm_pfam.md) — and notably it reuses the very base model your roadmap starts from.

### What they built

CFP-Gen extends DPLM's discrete diffusion with three conditioning modules, one per modality ([cfpgen_paper.md:218-250](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L218-L250)):

| Modality | Module | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **0D annotations** $c_\text{anno}$ (GO, IPR, EC) | **AGFM** — Annotation-Guided Feature Modulation | FiLM-style affine modulation of ESM block hidden states; one embedding per annotation type, summed, then produces $\gamma, \beta, \alpha$ |
| **1D sequence motifs** $c_\text{seq}$ | **RCFE** — Residue-Controlled Functional Encoder | ControlNet-style trainable *copy* of ESM blocks added to the frozen main branch via zero-init linear layers |
| **3D structure** $c_\text{str}$ | **GVPT** — GVP-Transformer | Cross-attention into the final ESM block; **directly reuses the pretrained DPLM cross-attention/adapter weights with no extra training** |

The three modules are composed sequentially ([eq:main, L243-247](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L243-L247)):

$$h = \mathcal{A}\big(f_\text{RCFE}(f_\text{AGFM}(\mathbf{x}^{(t)}, c_\text{anno}), c_\text{seq}),\ f_\text{GVPT}(c_\text{str})\big)$$

where $\mathcal{A}$ is a cross-attention layer. The system is built so any subset or combination of conditions can be supplied at inference.

### Annotation conditioning (AGFM) — most relevant to your Pfam plan

AGFM is the part most analogous to your family-prefix design ([L265-333](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L265-L333)):

- Uses **GO, IPR (InterPro), and EC** as the three primary annotation types. Pfam is explicitly mentioned as an extensible option ([L280](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L280)).
- Each annotation type gets a dedicated embedding layer; multi-label sets are summed into one vector: $\mathbf{c}_\text{GO} + \mathbf{c}_\text{IPR} + \mathbf{c}_\text{EC}$ ([L311](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L311)).
- The combined vector produces FiLM coefficients $\gamma, \beta, \alpha$ applied per ESM block ([L317-328](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L317-L328)).
- **Only the annotation embedding layers and one MLP layer are trained** — the DPLM backbone stays frozen ([L298-299](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L298-L299)).
- They contrast themselves with ESM3 (limited IPR vocab), ZymCTRL (EC only), ProteoGAN (GO only), and ProGen (multi-tag but needs per-task fine-tuning) ([L282-290](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L282-L290)).

### Motif conditioning (RCFE)

For residue-level constraints they use a dual-branch ControlNet design ([L335-403](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L335-L403)):

- Main branch (AGFM-augmented ESM) stays frozen.
- A trainable *copy* of the ESM blocks takes the motif (with non-motif positions `<mask>`-padded, projected via zero-init $\mathcal{F}_\text{in}$) and its output is added back via another zero-init $\mathcal{F}_\text{out}$ ([eq:control, L384](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L384)).
- Only the first half (encoder side) of ESM2 is used as the trainable copy for efficiency ([L396-397](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L396-L397)).
- Crucially, unlike DPLM/EvoDiff motif infilling which *fixes* motif residues, RCFE **dynamically updates** them during sampling to emulate evolution / discover improved motifs ([L348-352](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L348-L352)).

### Structure conditioning

Not a new module — they directly load DPLM's pretrained GVP-Transformer + cross-attention adapter (trained on CATH) without further training, and show it works plug-and-play ([L469-476](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L469-L476), [L518-520](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L518-L520)). They cite this as evidence that "more functional adapters can be incorporated."

### Composable inference and the new task they introduce

The combination objective defines **functional protein inverse folding** ("inverse function task", [L449-465](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L449-L465)):

$$\mathbf{x}^* = \arg\max_\mathbf{x}\ p(\mathbf{x} \mid c_\text{anno}, c_\text{seq}, c_\text{str}) + S_\text{func}(\mathbf{x}, c_\text{anno})$$

— i.e. recover the sequence for a given backbone *while also* hitting requested GO/IPR/EC labels. They frame this as reducing the search space to sequences that are simultaneously structurally viable and functionally relevant.

### Training recipe

- Base: pretrained **DPLM-650M** ([L512-513](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L512-L513)).
- Two-stage progressive training: (1) train AGFM, (2) train the RCFE copy blocks. Structure adapter is reused frozen ([L513-520](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L513-L520)).
- Datasets: 103,939 SwissProt sequences covering 375 GO terms + 1,154 IPR domains (general); 139,551 enzymes with 661 EC numbers (CARE-intersected); PDB + AFDB for backbones ([L496-510](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L496-L510)).

### Reported results (Tab. `[tab:sota_comparison]`, [L407-441](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L407-L441))

Conditioning is evaluated by running generated sequences back through function predictors (DeepGO-SE for GO, InterProScan for IPR, a learned classifier for EC). The ablation rows make the composable-multiple-condition thesis explicit — performance climbs monotonically as conditions are added. For the EC table for example: DPLM (sequence motif + structure only) achieves MRR 0.211 / mic-F1 0.241, while CFP-Gen with EC + GO + IPR + Motif reaches **MRR 0.924 / mic-F1 0.942**. They also claim a 30% F1 improvement over ESM3 ([L99-101](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L99-L101)).

### Relevance to your roadmap

This paper is highly relevant and is essentially a published instance of stages 4–7 of your [conditional_dplm_pfam_stages.md](plans/conditional_dplm_pfam_stages.md) (stronger conditioning, gradient/feature guidance, ProDVA-style function readiness, cross-attention), with three concrete takeaways:

1. **FiLM-style AGFM is a stronger baseline than soft prefix tokens** for annotation conditioning, and it's still a frozen-backbone design — your "prefix-only frozen DPLM" Run 1 ([conditional_dplm_pfam.md Run 1](plans/conditional_dplm_pfam.md)) could be compared directly against a CFP-Gen-style AGFM ablation.
2. **The DPLM cross-attention structure adapter transfers without retraining** — relevant to your Stage 6 cross-attention roadmap and to your existing [cond_dplm_*](src/byprot/models/dplm/modules/dplm_adapter.py) inverse-folding configs.
3. **Pfam is explicitly called out as an extensible AGFM annotation type** ([L280](/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/cfpgen_paper.md#L280)) — your Pfam-first plan is a strict subset of their annotation axis, so CFP-Gen is the natural primary baseline to beat (or to reproduce as a reference) when you reach the multi-annotation phase.

One caveat worth flagging against your evaluation strategy: CFP-Gen evaluates functionality with *neural function predictors* (DeepGO-SE, InterProScan, EC classifiers). Your [conditional_dplm_pfam.md](plans/conditional_dplm_pfam.md) is rightly adamant that HMMER/Pfam remains the primary metric for the family task — CFP-Gen's evaluation philosophy is exactly the "neural classifier only" approach your plan warns against in its "Reranker Over-Optimization" risk section.

## ProCALM vs CFP-Gen for conditional DPLM-2

The two are different conditioning mechanisms, not different qualities of the same mechanism. The question is which fits DPLM-2's architecture and your roadmap better.

### Mechanism comparison (grounded in actual code)

| Aspect | ProCALM `ParallelAdapterLayer` | CFP-Gen AGFM |
|---|---|---|
| **Where it attaches** | Parallel branch added at every transformer block; output summed into the residual stream *before* the residual connection ([model.py:333](../ProCALM/progen_conditional/model/model.py#L333), [adapter.py:178-225](../ProCALM/progen_conditional/model/adapter.py#L178-L225)) | FiLM modulation applied *inside* each layer at both LayerNorms + gated residuals ([esm_cfpgen.py:124-127, 197-201](../cfpgen/src/byprot/models/lm/esm_cfpgen.py#L124-L127)) |
| **Conditioning math** | Low-rank bottleneck: LN(h) → down-project → concat/sum with projected condition → MLP → up-project → near-zero init ([adapter.py:91-176](../ProCALM/progen_conditional/model/adapter.py#L91-L176)) | Per-layer adaLN producing 6 FiLM params (shift/scale/gate × 2) from a single annotation embedding |
| **Condition encoder** | `ProjectionMLP` per condition key, encoding raw EC one-hot / DRFP / CREEP / tax vectors to `c_s=128` ([adapter.py:7-45](../ProCALM/progen_conditional/model/adapter.py#L7-L45)) | `FuncTagEmbedder` — `nn.Embedding` lookup per annotation type, summed across types ([esm_cfpgen.py:210-223](../cfpgen/src/byprot/models/lm/esm_cfpgen.py#L210-L223)) |
| **Multi-condition** | Either shared adapter or separate parallel adapters summed (`ParallelAdapterLayer`) | Single summed embedding feeds one adaLN — composable for free |
| **Base model** | ProGen2 (causal LM) | DPLM (masked diffusion LM) |
| **Param count** | Per layer: `2 × c_h × c_hidden + small MLP` — with `c_h=1280, c_hidden=16`, ≈41k params × 33 layers ≈ 1.4M per condition | Per layer: `c_h × 6 × c_h` = 9.8M params × 33 layers ≈ **322M** (huge — but it's a *single shared* adaLN, so actually `c_h × 6 × c_h = 9.8M` total regardless of layer count, plus small embedding tables) |
| **Init** | Explicit near-zero weight init on `linear_up` (std=1e-5) so adapter is identity-like at start | Zero-init of `linear_up` in RCFE; AGFM relies on the gate being learnable |

### Why ProCALM's design actually fits DPLM-2 better

1. **Architecture match.** ProCALM's parallel-adapter pattern is *numerically additive on the residual stream* — it doesn't care what happens inside the transformer block. DPLM-2's `ModifiedEsmLayer` ([dplm2_modeling_esm.py:259-352](src/byprot/models/dplm2/modules/dplm2_modeling_esm.py#L259-L352)) has the rotary-embedding attention, dual-modality `type_ids`, and a specific `feed_forward_chunk` that CFP-Gen's AGFM wants to *replace* (it swaps `EsmLayer` → `AGFMLayer` end-to-end). ProCALM just *adds* an adapter module alongside the existing layer — no edits to the inner attention/FFN forward pass, no risk to the pretrained dual-stream rotary machinery.

2. **Frozen-base invariant is cleaner.** The ProCALM adapter is a strict *residual* with near-zero init; the base DPLM-2 forward graph is untouched. CFP-Gen's AGFM modifies LayerNorm → modulate → attention → modulate → FFN at *every* layer, which means "frozen base" requires the AGFM math to be provably identity at init. It is (zero shift/scale = identity, gate=0 → output residual dropped), but it requires the modified `ModifiedEsmLayer.forward` to exist, which is invasive. ProCALM keeps the layer file unchanged.

3. **Multi-condition composition is more principled.** ProCALM's `ParallelAdapterLayer` ([adapter.py:178-225](../ProCALM/progen_conditional/model/adapter.py#L178-L225)) stacks independent adapters per condition and sums them. CFP-Gen's AGFM collapses all annotations to one embedding via summation before a single adaLN — the conditions are not separable post-summation. ProCALM's design is what you'd want for the cross-attention-adapter future hook (one adapter for Pfam tags, one for retrieved fragments, one for text encoder) without them stepping on each other.

4. **Annotation encoders are interchangeable.** ProCALM already ships three: EC one-hot, DRFP reaction fingerprints, CREEP text embeddings. The interface is "project arbitrary fixed-dim vector → adapter input dim" via `ProjectionMLP`. CFP-Gen commits to discrete `nn.Embedding` lookups, which works for Pfam/GO/IPR/EC tags but doesn't naturally accept continuous retrievals or text-encoder outputs. ProCALM's interface is closer to what your Stage 5/6 (ProDVA-style retrieval, cross-attention memory) needs.

### Why CFP-Gen is still better on two axes

1. **Stronger conditioning at frozen base.** FiLM modulates *both* the attention pre-LN and the FFN pre-LN, plus gated residuals. ProCALM's parallel adapter adds a residual only — it doesn't change the layer's internal computation. For a *frozen* base, CFP-Gen's AGFM gives the condition more direct leverage over per-position hidden states. Empirically CFP-Gen reports strong results with a frozen DPLM backbone; ProCALM is usually trained with adapter-only fine-tuning, which is more flexible but not strictly frozen.

2. **Tested on a diffusion LM.** CFP-Gen runs on DPLM-1 (discrete diffusion). ProCALM runs on ProGen2 (autoregressive). Adapter behaviors differ between the two regimes — diffusion generates over many denoising steps where the adapter is applied repeatedly, while AR applies it once per token. CFP-Gen's authors have already validated this.

### Recommendation: hybrid — ProCALM-style parallel adapters as the primary, AGFM-FiLM as an option

Both mechanisms are small and orthogonal. The cleanest design is:

- **Primary: ProCALM-style parallel adapter** — `ParallelAdapterLayer` attached at every `ModifiedEsmLayer` (or a subset), residual-summed before the residual connection, near-zero init, condition-via-`ProjectionMLP`. Frozen base. This is the minimal-invasive surface that supports Pfam / GO / IPR / EC / retrieval / text uniformly, and gives you the cross-attention-adapter-style hook for free (it *is* an external-encoder adapter already).
- **Optional: AGFM-FiLM** — for users who want stronger per-layer conditioning at frozen base, add the FiLM modulation path as a config flag on `ModifiedEsmLayer`. Off by default.
- **Drop: the cross-attention adapter from the previous plan.** ProCALM's parallel adapter already serves the role of "external memory injected at every layer." A separate `CrossAttentionAdapterLayer` is redundant unless you specifically want token-level (not vector-level) memory.

## Summary

**ProCALM's parallel adapter is a better primary fit for DPLM-2 than CFP-Gen's AGFM**, but the two are complementary enough to ship both.

**Why ProCALM wins as the primary:**
- It's a strict residual on the post-block hidden state — DPLM-2's `ModifiedEsmLayer` (with its dual-stream rotary embeddings and `type_ids` plumbing) stays bit-for-bit untouched. AGFM has to *replace* the layer internals.
- Near-zero init on `linear_up` gives a clean identity-at-start guarantee.
- `ProjectionMLP` accepts arbitrary-dim vectors — Pfam/GO/IPR/EC embeddings, retrieved fragments, text-encoder outputs all use the same interface. AGFM's `nn.Embedding` lookups lock you to discrete tags.
- `ParallelAdapterLayer` gives separable multi-condition composition; AGFM collapses conditions into one summed embedding before a single adaLN.

**Where CFP-Gen still wins:**
- Stronger per-layer conditioning at strict frozen base (FiLM modulates both attention and FFN pre-LayerNorms; the adapter is residual-only).
- Actually validated on a diffusion LM (DPLM-1) vs ProCALM's autoregressive ProGen2.

**The plan reconciles both:**
- Primary: ProCALM-style `ParallelAdapterLayer` at every selected layer, fed by `ProjectionMLP`, fed in turn by a CFP-Gen-style `AnnotationEmbedder` for discrete Pfam/GO/IPR/EC tags.
- Optional `use_film` flag: ship the CFP-Gen AGFM math as an opt-in for users who need stronger frozen-base conditioning.
- Dropped: the separate cross-attention adapter from the earlier draft. ProCALM's parallel adapter already serves as the "external-memory-injected-per-layer" hook — a dedicated `CrossAttentionAdapterLayer` is redundant unless you specifically need token-level (not vector-level) memory.

One residual risk worth flagging clearly: ProCALM was validated with adapter-only fine-tuning (base frozen, but the adapters are a meaningful fraction of trainable params). At strict frozen base with near-zero init, the adapter signal may be weak on the first run. The escape hatch is the FiLM flag, or unfreezing the adapters' `linear_up`/`ProjectionMLP` more aggressively.

# CFP-Gen vs. DPLM-2: Methodology Comparison for Adding a "Function"/Multimodal Capability to a Protein LM

## 1. CFP-Gen's methodology for the function-annotation modality

### 1a. AGFM (Annotation-Guided Feature Modulation) — FiLM-style per-layer modulation

**Paper (cfpgen_paper.md §3.2, lines 265-333):** For each annotation type (GO, IPR, EC), a dedicated embedding layer is maintained; each tag is mapped to a same-dimensional vector and the embeddings are **summed** (`x_anno = f_AGFM(x, c_GO, c_IPR, c_EC)`, lines 304-308). The summed embedding is passed through a single MLP `F` to regress three parameters:
- `γ, β, α = F(c_GO + c_IPR + c_EC)` (line 311) — **scale (γ), shift (β), gate (α)**.
- Scale/shift modulate the normalized feature before SA and FFN: `x_out = γ ⊙ x + β` (line 324). This is FiLM de-normalization.
- Gate operates on the SA/FFN output: `x̂_out = α ⊙ x'_out + x'_out` (line 328).
- Specialized init (lines 315-319): weights predicting γ and β are **zero-initialized**; weights predicting α are **ones-initialized**.
- "CFP-Gen is achieved by training only the annotation embedding layers and a single MLP layer" (lines 298-299).

**Code (`esm_cfpgen.py`):**
- `FuncTagEmbedder` (lines 210-222): per-type `nn.Embedding(num_classes + 1, hidden_size)` (the +1 slot is a CFG/dropout placeholder).
- Per-type embedders instantiated in `CFPGenEncoder.__init__` for `go_embedder`, `ipr_embedder`, `ec_embedder` (lines 238, 244, 250).
- `drop_anno_ids` (lines 265-289): handles sample-level + per-tag dropout and explicitly **combines class embeddings by summation** (`return torch.sum(torch.stack(class_embeds, dim=0), dim=0)`, line 289).
- Forward (lines 329-344): GO/IPR/EC embeddings are computed independently and added: `anno_embed = anno_embed + ipr_embed if anno_embed is not None else ipr_embed`.
- `AGFMLayer` (lines 148-207): `adaLN_modulation = nn.Sequential(nn.SiLU(), nn.Linear(hidden_size, 6 * hidden_size))` (lines 158-161) — **6 modulation params per layer**, chunked into `(shift_msa, scale_msa, gate_msa, shift_mlp, scale_mlp, gate_mlp)` (line 177).
- `modulate(x, shift, scale) = x * (1 + scale.unsqueeze(1)) + shift.unsqueeze(1)` (lines 52-53) — FiLM shift/scale.
- Gating in `AGFMSelfOutput`/`AGFMOutput`: `hidden_states = gate.unsqueeze(1) * hidden_states + input_tensor` (lines 66-67, 77-78).
- Init in `ModifiedEsmModel._init_weights` (lines 478-485): zero the adaLN weight and the shift/scale biases (`bias[:2*H]`, `bias[3*H:5*H]`), ones the gate biases (`bias[2*H:3*H]`, `bias[5*H:6*H]`). This matches the paper's "γ,β → 0; α → 1" prescription, applied separately for SA and FFN halves.

So: **6 modulation parameters per layer** (the paper's prose describes the generic 3-parameter γ/β/α form; the code generates distinct γ/β/α sets for the self-attention sublayer and the FFN sublayer).

### 1b. RCFE (Residue-Controlled Functional Encoder) — ControlNet-style trainable copy

**Paper (§3.3, lines 335-403):** A second, trainable branch of modified ESM blocks is added. The main branch `E_esm(·, Θ_esm)` stays **frozen**; the second branch `E_seq(·, Θ_seq)` is a **trainable copy** of `Θ_esm`. The motif is padded with `&lt;mask&gt;`, projected into the latent space (`c_seq ∈ R^{L×D}`), and combined via:
`x_seq = E_esm(x; Θ_esm) + F_out(E_seq(x + F_in(c_seq; Θ_in); Θ_seq); Θ_out)` (Eq. 6, line 384).
- `F_in` and `F_out` are **zero-initialized linear layers** (lines 385-391) — enabling gradual incorporation of the motif condition.
- "we leverage only the first half blocks of the ESM2 model to encode sequence motifs" (lines 396-398).
- **Differs from DPLM's motif infilling**: DPLM/EvoDiff "rely on fixed amino acids throughout generation, RCFE dynamically updates the specified motifs during inference" (lines 346-352) — emulating evolution rather than hard-fixing residues.

**Code (`esm_cfpgen.py`):**
- `RCFEBlock` (lines 21-49): `self.copied_block = deepcopy(base_block)` (line 25) — the trainable copy. `before_proj` exists only for `block_index == 0`, both `before_proj` and `after_proj` are **zero-initialized** (`nn.init.zeros_(...)`, lines 31-32, 35-36).
- `CFPGenEncoder.__init__` (lines 255-260): `copy_blocks_num = config.num_hidden_layers // 2` (first half of the ESM blocks); `seq_controlnet = nn.ModuleList([RCFEBlock(AGFMLayer(...), i, ...) for i in range(copy_blocks_num)])`.
- Forward (lines 363-374): the controller runs the copy blocks; the main branch layer at index `i` receives `hidden_states + motif_skip` and is modulated by `random_go_embed`. Main-branch AGFM layers also remain frozen in the sense that only the AGFM embeddings/MLP + the copy blocks + zero-init projections are trained.

### 1c. GVPT (GVP-Transformer) for the STRUCTURE modality — reuses DPLM-1's cross-attention adapter

**Paper (§3.4, lines 467-480):** Structure is encoded by `f_GVPT` (GVP-Transformer, Hsu et al. 2022) into `c_str`, then "c_str is injected into the **final ESM block** of the main branch through a **cross-attention layer**, following the strategy of DPLM." Key passage (lines 473-476): *"In our implementation, we found that the pretrained cross-attention layer from DPLM could be directly utilized **without the need of further training**, suggesting that more functional adapters can be incorporated."* Reinforced in Implementation Details (lines 518-521): *"we directly use the GVP-Transformer and structure adapter from DPLM, which are pretrained on the CATH database, **without additional fine-tuning** for CFP-Gen."*

**Code (`modules/dplm_adapter.py` + `modules/gvp_transformer_encoder.py`):**
- `GVPTransformerEncoderWrapper` (gvp_transformer_encoder.py, lines 12-40): loads `esm.pretrained.esm_if1_gvp4_t16_142M_UR50()` and uses its `.encoder`; **frozen by default** (`freeze=True`, lines 17-19). This is DPLM-1's structure encoder.
- `AdapterLayer` (dplm_adapter.py, lines 159-246): replaces the last ESM layer. Contains a standard self-attention/FFN path **plus** a cross-attention adapter: `self.adapter_crossattention = ModifiedEsmAttention(config, kdim=kdim, vdim=vdim)` (lines 170-172), with `kdim=vdim=encoder_d_model=512` (the GVP feature dim). The forward (lines 220-234) runs `adapter_crossattention(hidden_states=layer_output, encoder_hidden_states=encoder_hidden_states)` then an FFN with residual.
- `DPLMWithConditionalAdatper.from_pretrained` (lines 40-60): the adapter is loaded from the pretrained DPLM last-layer weights (`adapter.load_state_dict(net_last_layer.state_dict(), strict=False)`, line 48), and **all non-adapter params are frozen** (`if 'adapter' not in pname: param.requires_grad = False`, lines 56-57).

### 1d. Composition of the three modules and conditioning target

**Paper (Eq. 4 "main", lines 243-250):**
`h(x^(t), c) = A( f_RCFE( f_AGFM(x^(t), c_anno), c_seq ),  f_GVPT(c_str) )`
where `A` is the cross-attention layer (the structure adapter). The conditioning target is the prediction of the clean sequence `x̂^(0)` via `Softmax(W h)` (Eq. 3, lines 242-243). The conditioning target is **the amino-acid sequence only** — function/structure/sequence-motif are all conditions; the model never generates them. Training objective (Eq. 5, lines 255-256) is weighted cross-entropy with a condition-strength gate γ(c) controlled by dropout.

**Code composition (`cfp_gen.py` + `esm_cfpgen.py`):** `CondDiffusionProteinLanguageModel.compute_loss` (cfpgen.py lines 256-299) builds `inputs = dict(x_t=x_t, seq_cond=masked_target, go=..., ipr=..., ec=...)` and calls `self.forward(inputs)`, which dispatches to `EsmForCFPGEN` → `ModifiedEsmModel` → `CFPGenEncoder.forward`, where AGFM, RCFE, and (via the final adapter layer) the GVPT cross-attention all run inside the single ESM encoder pass.

---

## 2. DPLM-2's LFQ-tokenizer methodology for the structure modality

### 2a. Central architectural decision: structure as native tokens in one self-attention stream

**Paper (dplm2_paper.md §3.1, lines 264-313):** Structure is converted into a discrete token sequence `z = (z_1, …, z_L)` via a tokenizer; DPLM-2 "processes multimodal input by **concatenating** the structure token sequence `z` with the corresponding amino acid sequence `s`." There is a "position-by-position correspondence between `z` and `s`," and identical position encodings are assigned to both `z_i` and `s_i` (lines 285-290). The joint objective (Eq., lines 301-303) learns `p_θ(z_i, s_i | z^(t), s^(t))` with `log p(z_i,s_i|·) = log p(z_i|·) + log p(s_i|·)`, enabling "simultaneous generation … in a single step" — explicitly "**eliminating the need for a cascaded generation paradigm**" (lines 308-312). The framing of the whole paper (lines 28-54) is "build a multimodal protein foundation model to **simultaneously model, understand, and generate** both sequences and structures."

### 2b. The LFQ structure tokenizer (encoder / quantizer / decoder)

**Paper (§3.3, lines 353-419):** The tokenizer follows a VQ-VAE-style pipeline `x →[encoder] e →[quantizer] z →[decoder] x̃`. Encoder = GVP-based structure encoder from pre-trained GVP-Transformer (Jing/Hsu), **frozen** during tokenizer training (paper §Structure Tokenizer, lines 855-860). Quantizer = **Lookup-Free Quantizer** (LFQ, Yu et al. 2023): the latent space is the Cartesian product of single-dimensional binary variables `C = ×_{k=1}^{log2|Z|} C_k`, `C_k = {-1, 1}` (lines 390-396). Each dim is quantized by `sign(e_i[k])`; the token index is the binary encoding `z_i = Σ 2^{k-1} 1{e_i[k] &gt; 0}` (lines 396-399). Decoder = IPA-based (AlphaFold2) with 4 EvoFormer layers (no MSA row attention, following ESMFold) (paper §Structure Tokenizer, lines 863-867). Trained with reconstruction (FAPE + violation + distogram) + commitment + entropy regularization losses (lines 400-404, 870-879). "**a codebook size of 8192 achieves the best compression-reconstruction trade-off**" (lines 411-412).

**Code (`structok_lfq.py`):** `VQModel` (lines 32-104) composes `self.encoder = Encoder(**encoder_config)` (GVP), `self.quantize = LFQ(dim=embed_dim, codebook_size=num_codes, …)` (lines 58-63), `self.decoder = Decoder(**decoder_config)` (ESMFold-style IPA, line 56). Forward (lines 113-136): `pre_quant, encoder_feats = self.encode(...)`, `quant, loss, (_, _, struct_tokens) = self.quantize(pre_quant, …)`, `decoder_out = self.decode(quant, …)`.

**Code (`modules/lfq.py`):** `LFQ` class (lines 133+). Asserts codebook size is a power of 2 (lines 153-155); `self.codebook_dim = int(log2(codebook_size))` (line 158). Quantization is sign-based: `quantized = torch.where(x &gt; 0, 1.0, -1.0)` (lines 293-296). `bits_to_indices` (lines 241-255) and `indices_to_bits` (lines 205-216) do the binary ↔ index conversion. Entropy loss (`entropy_loss`, lines 95-130) uses softmax temperature 0.01 with sample-minimization + batch-maximization weights.

**Config (`configs/experiment/structok/structok_lfq_8k_pdb_swissprot_c512.yaml`):** `num_codes: 8192 # 2^13`, `embed_dim: 13` (lines 54-55). **Codebook 8192 = 2^13, 13-bit binary {-1, +1}** confirmed. All DPLM-2 experiment configs (`dplm2_150m/650m/3b/bit_650m/650m_selfmixup.yaml`) set `struct_vocab_size: 8192`.

### 2c. AA + struct token concatenation, shared embedding table, modality distinction, per-half rotary

**Concatenation:** `dplm2.py` `compute_loss` (line 403): `x_t = torch.concat([struct_noised["x_t"], aatype_noised["x_t"]], dim=1)` — **[struct | aa] along the sequence dimension**. The decoder also chunks the logits back into struct/aa halves (line 419): `struct_logits, aatype_logits = model_outputs["logits"].chunk(2, dim=1)`.

**Single shared embedding table:** `dplm2.py` `forward` (lines 258-261): `input_embeds = self.net.esm.embeddings(input_ids, attention_mask=input_mask)` — one embedding lookup for both modalities. The unified vocab is `33 (AA tokens) + 8192 (struct tokens) + 4 (special struct tokens)` (`TokenizerConfig`, lines 32-34).

**`get_modality_type` — distinguish by token-id range (lines 220-227):** `modality_type = ((input_ids &lt; 33) &amp; input_mask).int()` with an explicit HACK comment: *"all amino acid token id &lt; 33, while all struct token id &gt;= 33; 0 stands for struct, 1 stands for aa, 2 stands for padding."* The same id-range trick is reused in `forward_decoder` (lines 507-509) to mask logits: `logits[..., :33] = -inf` at struct positions and `logits[..., 33:] = -inf` at aa positions.

**`ModifiedRotaryEmbedding` per-half split (`dplm2_modeling_esm.py`, lines 28-85):** When both `aa_type` and `struct_type` are present, the effective sequence length is halved (`seq_len /= 2`, line 43) and the query/key are each `chunk(2, dim=-2)` into struct-half and aa-half, with the **same** cos/sin tables applied to both halves (lines 71-79), then re-concatenated. This enforces the position-by-position correspondence between `z_i` and `s_i` described in the paper.

### 2d. The four training modes via masking + attention bias

**Code (`dplm2.py`, `construct_x_t` lines 317-392 and `forward` lines 229-270):** Five ratios (summing to 1.0, asserted at line 333-340) partition the batch — `single_modality_ratio`, `folding_loss_ratio`, `inverse_folding_loss_ratio`, `independent_loss_ratio`, `joint_loss_ratio` (default config: 0.25 / 0.25 / 0.25 / 0.0 / 0.25, dplm2_650m.yaml lines 30-34). Each mode is realized by separately sampling diffusion timesteps for struct and AA and zeroing one of them:
- **single_modality:** the `single_modality_index` subset gets an attention-bias block (lines 243-256) that masks struct rows from attending to AA columns and vice versa (`struct_attention_bias[…, :, :, L//2:] = -inf`, `aa_attention_bias[…, :, :, :L//2] = -inf`) — the two modalities are denoised independently.
- **folding** (`folding_index`): `aatype_t` is forced to 0 (AA stays clean) while struct is noised (line 378) — learn `p(z|s)`.
- **inverse_folding** (`inverse_folding_index`): `struct_t` is forced to 0 (struct stays clean) while AA is noised (line 370) — learn `p(s|z)`.
- **joint** (`joint_index`): struct and AA share the same timestep (`aatype_t = struct_t` on the joint subset, line 379) — learn `p(z, s)` jointly.

Distinct noise schedulers per modality (paper §3.1, lines 314-319): the design "allows us to explore arbitrary combinations of (t_z, t_s)."

### 2e. No cross-attention in DPLM-2

The `ModifiedEsmLayer` still inherits a `crossattention` submodule guarded by `if self.add_cross_attention:` (`dplm2_modeling_esm.py` lines 266, 313-345) — standard ESM inheritance. But: (i) `add_cross_attention` is never set true in any DPLM-2 config (confirmed absent in `dplm2_650m.yaml`); (ii) `dplm2.py` `forward` (lines 263-268) calls `self.net(input_ids=…, inputs_embeds=…, attention_mask=…, type_ids=…)` and **never passes `encoder_hidden_states`**, so `is_cross_attention` in `ModifiedEsmSelfAttention` (line 111) is always False. Structure and sequence interact purely through standard self-attention over the concatenated token stream. **There is no cross-attention in DPLM-2 in practice.**

---

## 3. The direct methodological contrast (side-by-side)

| Dimension | **CFP-Gen** (function = side-channel condition) | **DPLM-2** (structure = native token) |
|---|---|---|
| **Non-sequence modality: representation** | **Function** = continuous condition vector: per-type `nn.Embedding` for GO/IPR/EC, summed, then FiLM γ/β/α (esm_cfpgen.py L158-161, L210-222, L289). **Structure** = external GVP-Transformer encoder producing continuous features, injected via cross-attention adapter (dplm_adapter.py L170-172; gvp_transformer_encoder.py L15). | **Structure** = native **discrete token** in a unified vocab (33 AA + 8192 struct + 4 special). Tokenized upstream by a frozen LFQ tokenizer (structok_lfq.py; lfq.py). |
| **Where the modality enters the network** | **Per-layer FiLM modulation** of every AGFM block (6 adaLN params/layer, esm_cfpgen.py L177) + ControlNet-style trainable copy of the first-half ESM blocks for motif (RCFEBlock, L21-49) + **cross-attention at the final adapter layer** only (dplm_adapter.py L220-234). | **Input token sequence**: `[struct | aa]` concatenated along seq dim (dplm2.py L403), looked up in **one shared embedding table** (L258-261), processed by **standard self-attention**. Modality distinguished by token-id range &lt;33 / ≥33 (`get_modality_type` L220-227). |
| **Generative vs. conditioning** | Function (and structure, and motif) are **CONDITIONS only**. The model's sole output is `p(x̂^(0) | x^(t), c)` for the amino-acid sequence (Eq. 3-4, cfpgen_paper.md L242-250). **It cannot generate function, structure, or motif** — these are inputs. | Structure is **GENERATIVE**. The model learns `p(z_i, s_i | ·)` and co-generates seq+struct (dplm2_paper.md L301-312). Enables any-to-any: folding, inverse folding, joint co-generation, motif scaffolding. |
| **Backbone retraining** | **Frozen backbone + trained adapters.** Main ESM blocks frozen; only AGFM embedding/MLP, RCFE copy blocks + zero-init projections, and (optionally) the SFT structure adapter are trained (dplm_adapter.py L56-57; cfpgen_paper.md L298-299). The GVPT structure adapter can even be reused **without any training** (cfpgen_paper.md L473-476, L518-521). | **Whole model is (re)trained.** `training_stage: train_from_dplm` — pretrained DPLM weights initialize, then continued training on the unified vocab with **LoRA** (lora.enable: true, rank 16, dplm2_650m.yaml L37-43) to limit forgetting. |
| **Loss** | `RDMCrossEntropyLoss` (configs/experiment/lm/cond_dplm_650m.yaml L49) = label-smoothed NLL / weighted cross-entropy on AA tokens (cross_entropy.py L155-191). **No contrastive / InfoNCE term.** | `StructAARDMCrossEntropyLoss` (dplm2_650m.yaml L63-64) = label-smoothed NLL cross-entropy applied **separately** to struct logits and aa logits, then summed (cross_entropy.py L246-320). **No contrastive / InfoNCE term.** |
| **Position handling** | Standard ESM rotary over the sequence; structure enters via cross-attention so it carries no positional conflict. | `ModifiedRotaryEmbedding` halves the sequence length and applies the **same** cos/sin to the struct half and the aa half so `z_i` and `s_i` share position `i` (dplm2_modeling_esm.py L40-80). |
| **Tokenization offload** | None for function (embedding lookup); structure tokenizer (GVPT) is a separate frozen encoder reused from DPLM-1. | A **separate, independently trained LFQ tokenizer** (structok_lfq.py) must be trained first (2 days on 8 A100s, paper §3.3 L408-410) and frozen afterward. |

---

## 4. One-paragraph synthesis

The slide's punchline is an architectural-strategy fork. **CFP-Gen treats function exactly the way DPLM-1 treated structure** — as a *side-channel condition*: a continuous vector encoded by an external module, injected into a **frozen** backbone through per-layer FiLM modulation (AGFM) and a single cross-attention adapter (the GVPT/DPLM-1 structure adapter, reused without retraining). The model conditions on function/structure/motif but **never generates** them; its only output distribution is over amino acids. **DPLM-2 is precisely the upgrade away from that pattern**: it removes cross-attention entirely and instead **tokenizes structure into the same discrete vocabulary** as amino acids (LFQ, 8192 codes, 13-bit), concatenates `[struct | aa]` as one input stream into standard self-attention, and **retrains the whole model** (from DPLM init, with LoRA) so that structure becomes a **first-class generative** modality — enabling any-to-any co-generation. Both use pure diffusion cross-entropy; neither adds contrastive/InfoNCE. The natural question for our project is therefore: **should function follow the CFP-Gen adapter path** (fast, frozen-base, non-generative — bolt a FiLM/ControlNet/cross-attention condition onto a frozen DPLM) **or the DPLM-2 tokenization path** (slower — requires training a function tokenizer and retraining the backbone — but yields a unified, generative, multimodal model where function, structure, and sequence are all native tokens)? CFP-Gen's own paper hints at the limitation of its choice: it lists "sequence–structure co-design should be incorporated" and "enriching the scope of functional annotations" as future work (cfpgen_paper.md L771-776), and notes that its annotation vocabulary is a fixed, closed set — exactly the rigidity that a token-based approach removes.</result>

# DPLM / DPLM-2 / CFP-Gen Training-Data Facts

## 1. DPLM (sequence-only) training data

**Corpus.** UniRef50 (clustered at 50% sequence identity). The DPLM-2 paper states the size directly: *"our structure dataset is significantly smaller than UniRef50 sequence database (200K vs. 45M)"* — i.e. **~45M clusters/sequences** (`dplm2_paper.md:345-346`).

**Single training example.** Just a consensus amino-acid sequence string — no structure, no function labels. `UniRefDataset.__getitem__` reads one line from `consensus.fasta` and returns it untokenized (`src/byprot/datamodules/dataset/uniref.py:217-230`). The `DPLMCollater` then wraps each sequence with the ESM tokenizer (`facebook/esm2_t30_150M_UR50D`) producing `input_ids`, `input_mask`, `targets` (`uniref.py:257-286`). On-disk layout of the data folder: `consensus.fasta`, `splits.json` (`train`/`valid`/`test` index lists), `lengths_and_offsets.npz` (`uniref.py:184-209`).

**Datamodule/config.**
- Wrapper: `UniRefDataModule` (`src/byprot/datamodules/uniref50.py`), registered as `uniref50`.
- HF wrapper: `UniRefHFDataModule` (`uniref50_hf.py`), registered as `uniref50_hf`.
- Defaults (`configs/datamodule/uniref50.yaml`, `uniref50_hf.yaml`): `max_tokens: 6000`, `max_len: 1022`, `num_workers: 8`.

## 2. DPLM-2 training data

### 2a. Sources, sizes, filtering

**Two sources combined into one CSV (`pdb_swissprot`)** (`dplm2_paper.md:292-296, 804-820`):
- **Experimental PDB** — ~20K clustered experimental structures ("20K clustered experimental structures from the Protein Data Bank (PDB)").
- **AFDB SwissProt split** — ~200K AlphaFold-predicted structures from the AFDB SwissProt split (`varadi2022alphafold`).

Paper text: *"The training set of DPLM-2 is composed by experimental data, i.e.e, PDB, and high quality synthetic data, i.e.e, SwissProt. ... After filtering, the overall training set contains approximately 200,000 proteins. We limit the maximum length of the training set to 512."* (`dplm2_paper.md:806-814`).

**Filtering as documented in the paper (`dplm2_paper.md:806-820`):**
- SwissProt filtered to **avg pLDDT &gt; 85**.
- Max length **512** (longer proteins randomly cropped; 50% of batches randomly crop long proteins short for diversity).
- **Low-pLDDT (&lt;50) end segments cropped** from SwissProt proteins.

**Filtering actually applied in code** (`src/byprot/datamodules/dataset/tokenized_protein.py:28-95`, `preprocess_dataset`):
- Both AFDB and PDB rows pass through `remove_lowconf_ends(row, threshold=70)` — **end-cropping uses pLDDT threshold 70, not 50** as the paper says (`tokenized_protein.py:56-62`). This is the discrepancy to flag.
- AFDB rows additionally filtered by `plddt_std &lt; 15` (per-protein pLDDT variance cap).
- Length filter `aa_seq.str.len() &lt;= 1024` (the runtime cap is then imposed by `max_len=512`).
- Final keep rule: `split == "pdb"` **OR** (`avg_plddt` not null **AND** `avg_plddt &gt; 85`) (`tokenized_protein.py:69-75`). The 85 threshold matches the paper.
- `cameo2022` split held out as validation.

### 2b. What a single DPLM-2 training example contains

`TokenizedProteinDataset.__getitem__` (`tokenized_protein.py:282-320`) returns **only two modalities, both discrete**:
- `struct_tokens`: the precomputed LFQ **structure-token** string (field `struct_seq`, comma-separated integer codes, codebook size 8192), wrapped with `&lt;cls_struct&gt; ... &lt;eos_struct&gt;`.
- `aatype_tokens`: the amino-acid sequence (field `aa_seq`), wrapped with `&lt;cls_aa&gt; ... &lt;eos_aa&gt;`.
- `length` (= cropped length + 2 for the special tokens); optionally `pdb_name`.

**Important correction to the task framing: raw 3D coordinates are NOT part of the DPLM-2 LM training example.** The DPLM-2 language model never sees continuous coordinates — it operates purely on discrete struct tokens + aatype tokens. Coordinates are used (i) upstream, to **train the LFQ structure tokenizer** (see §2e below), and (ii) downstream, to **decode** predicted struct tokens back to coords at inference. The `DPLM2Collater` (`tokenized_protein.py:561-607`) batches only `struct_tokens.targets`, `struct_tokens.attention_mask`, `aatype_tokens.targets`, `aatype_tokens.attention_mask` (and optional `pdb_name`) — no coord tensors.

### 2c. Loss mixture

Implemented in `DPLM2.compute_loss -&gt; construct_x_t` (`src/byprot/models/dplm2/dplm2.py:322-399`). Each batch is randomly partitioned into **five** sub-batches (the fifth, `independent`, is set to 0 in all released configs):

| Sub-batch | Default ratio (`dplm2_650m.yaml:31-35`) | What is noised | What is clean / shared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `single_modality` | 0.25 | struct and aatype each noised at independent random `t` | — |
| `folding` | 0.25 | struct tokens (`t_z` sampled) | aatype clean (`t_s = 0`) — predict struct from seq |
| `inverse_folding` | 0.25 | aatype tokens (`t_s` sampled) | struct clean (`t_z = 0`) — predict seq from struct |
| `independent` | **0.0** (default in code is 0.0; `dplm2.py:61`) | (disabled) | both noised at independent t |
| `joint` | 0.25 | both modalities noised at the **same** timestep (`t_s := t_z`) | co-generation |

The ratios are asserted to sum to 1.0 (`dplm2.py:333-340`). So the user's "0.25 each" is correct **because `independent_loss_ratio=0.0`** — the four active sub-batches fill the batch. The mechanism: `struct_t.masked_fill(inverse_folding_index, 0)` makes struct clean for IF samples; `aatype_t.masked_fill(folding_index, 0)` makes aatype clean for folding samples; `aatype_t.masked_scatter(joint_index, struct_t[joint_index])` copies struct's timestep onto aatype for joint samples (`dplm2.py:377-388`). Every sub-batch contains the same `(struct_tokens, aatype_tokens)` pair from the same proteins — only the noise schedule differs.

### 2d. On-disk location and config defaults

- **Data file:** local `data_dir/pdb_swissprot.csv` (with `csv_file: pdb_swissprot`); the preprocessed HF-cached snapshot is written under `data_dir/pdb_swissprot/` with `train` and `valid` splits (`tokenized_protein.py:263-270, 90-92`). The LM vocab/tokenizer HF repo is `airkingbd/dplm2_650m` (`configs/datamodule/tokenized_protein.yaml:9`; `dplm2_650m.yaml:24, 27`). The pre-trained sequence backbone is loaded from `airkingbd/dplm_650m` (`dplm2_650m.yaml:42-44`).
- **DPLM-2 LM config defaults** (`configs/experiment/dplm2/dplm2_650m.yaml`): `max_tokens: 4000`, **`max_len: 512`**, `num_diffusion_timesteps: 500`, `struct_vocab_size: 8192`, LoRA enabled (rank 16), max_steps 100k, lr 1e-4. Identical `0.25/0.25/0.25/0.25/0.0` ratios in all four model sizes (`dplm2_150m/650m/3b.yaml`, `dplm2_650m_selfmixup.yaml`, `dplm2_bit_650m.yaml`).
- **Datamodule-level defaults** (`configs/datamodule/tokenized_protein.yaml`): `max_tokens: 6000`, `max_len: 1022`, `length_crop: true`, `cluster_training: false`, `min_crop_length: 60` — these are overridden by the experiment config above.

### 2e. Structure-tokenizer (LFQ) training data — same corpus

The LFQ struct tokenizer is trained on the **same PDB + AFDB-SwissProt pool, ~200K proteins** (`dplm2_paper.md:847-851`: *"trained using the same structure data as our multimodal language model, containing both experimental and high-quality structures, totaling 200K proteins"*). This is the path that **does** use continuous 3D backbone coords. Config: `configs/experiment/structok/structok_lfq_8k_pdb_swissprot_c512.yaml` — `train_split: [pdb, afdb_swissprot]`, `valid_split: [cameo2022]`, `csv_path: metadata.pdb_afdb_cameo.plddt.structok_lfq.csv`, `crop_size: 512`, `num_codes: 8192`, `embed_dim: 13`, `min_len: 60`, `allowed_oligomer: [monomeric]`, `max_loop_percent: 0.5`, `rog_quantile: 0.96`.

## 3. CFP-Gen training data

### 3a. General protein dataset

- **Size: 103,939 protein sequences covering 375 GO terms and 1,154 IPR domains** (`cfpgen_paper.md:501-504, 870-871`).
- **Source:** sequences from the **manually-curated Swiss-Prot subset of UniProtKB**; GO terms (focusing on molecular function) from UniProtKB/GO; IPR domain annotations from **InterPro** (`cfpgen_paper.md:497-500, 856-854`).
- **Frequency filter:** only GO and IPR terms with **≥ 100 annotated sequences** are retained ("as suggested by ProteoGAN") (`cfpgen_paper.md:859-862`).
- Confirmed in datamodule config `configs/datamodule/uniprotKB.yaml`: `data_dir: ${paths.data_dir}/uniprotKB/cfpgen_general_dataset`, and in `cfpgen_650m_stage1.yaml:30-31` (`go_num: 375`, `ipr_num: 1154`, `use_ec: false`).

### 3b. Enzyme design dataset

- **Size: 139,551 enzyme sequences spanning 661 EC numbers (4-level EC annotations)** (`cfpgen_paper.md:504-505, 916-919`).
- **Source:** **SwissProt ∩ CARE**. CARE (`yang2024care`) contributes 185,995 level-4-EC-annotated sequences; intersecting with Swiss-Prot (for GO/IPR compatibility) yields 139,551 / 661 EC labels (`cfpgen_paper.md:914-919`).
- Confirmed in `cfpgen_enzyme_650m.yaml:30-37` (`go_num: 780`, `ipr_num: 4982`, `ec_num: 661`, `use_ec: true`, `ec_drop: 0`); the alternate `data_dir: ${paths.data_dir}/uniprotKB/cfpgen_enzyme_dataset` is commented in `configs/datamodule/uniprotKB.yaml:4`.

### 3c. What a single CFP-Gen training example contains

`UniProtKBDataset.__getitem__` (`cfpgen/src/byprot/datamodules/dataset/uniprotKB.py:188-212`) returns a 5-tuple:
```
(consensus, go_type, ipr_type, ec_type, motif_start_end)
```
- `consensus` — the amino-acid sequence (cropped to `max_len`).
- `go_type` — list of integer GO-label IDs (from `go_f_mapped` or `go_mapped` field).
- `ipr_type` — list of integer IPR-label IDs (from `ipr_mapped`, default `[]`).
- `ec_type` — list of integer EC-label IDs (from `EC_mapped`, default `[]`).
- `motif_start_end` — `[motif['start'], motif['end']]` for the first IPR-derived motif, or `[0, 0]` if absent.

**Collator output** (`DPLMCollater.__call__`, `uniprotKB.py:271-318`) produces a batch dict with:
- `input_ids`, `input_mask`, `targets` — sequence tokens via ESM tokenizer.
- `go_type`, `ipr_type` — **multi-hot integer-ID lists, padded with -1 to the longest list in the batch**, then tensorized (`uniprotKB.py:300-306`):
  ```python
  padded_go_type = [go_list + [-1] * (max_go_len - len(go_list)) for go_list in go_type]
  ```
- `ec_type` — same -1-padding scheme (only if any EC labels are present, else list of empty lists) (`uniprotKB.py:283-291`).
- `motif_start_end` — `torch.tensor` of `(start, end)` pairs.

**Optional backbone structure** is **not loaded by this datamodule**. Backbone N/CA/C/O coordinates are loaded only on the inverse-folding / SFT path (`uniprotKB_if.py:30-59`): `UniProtKBInvFold` reads per-protein `.npy` coord arrays from `../uniprot_bb_coords/{uniprot_id}.npy`, validates `total_coords % 4 == 0` for the 4 backbone atoms, and the IF collator stacks them as `coords` of shape `L x n_atoms x 3` (`uniprotKB_if.py:74-194`). So for CFP-Gen: stage-1/stage-2 (general &amp; enzyme) examples carry **sequence + GO/IPR/EC label lists + motif span**, and the SFT/IF examples additionally carry **per-residue backbone coords**.

### 3d. Source of structure for CFP-Gen

Backbone coordinates are retrieved from **PDB and AlphaFold DB (AFDB)** — the same two sources as DPLM-2's structure data. From the appendix (`cfpgen_paper.md:891-896`): *"for each retained protein sequence, we retrieve its corresponding structural information from PDB and AlphaFold DB (AFDB) databases. Specifically, we extract the backbone atomic coordinates of 'N', 'CA', 'C', and 'O' and used them as structure condition."* The structure encoder itself is a GVP-Transformer reused from DPLM (pretrained on CATH), used without further fine-tuning except for an optional SFT adapter (`cfpgen_paper.md:511-524`, `670-689`).

## 4. Side-by-side dataset table

| Dataset | Source DB(s) | # Sequences | Attached to each sequence | Used to train |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DPLM (UniRef50)** | UniRef50 (clustered at 50%) | **~45M** | **Sequence only** (consensus AA string) | DPLM sequence pretraining (150M/650M/3B) |
| **DPLM-2 (PDB+AFDB-SwissProt)** | Experimental PDB (clustered) + AFDB SwissProt predicted | **~220K total** (~20K PDB + ~200K AFDB-SwissProt, after pLDDT&gt;85 / len≤512 filtering) | **Sequence + per-residue LFQ structure tokens (codebook 8192)** — discrete only, no coords at the LM level | DPLM-2 sequence–structure co-generation (folding / inverse-folding / joint / single-modality) |
| **DPLM-2 struct tokenizer (same corpus)** | PDB + AFDB-SwissProt | ~200K | Continuous backbone N/CA/C/O 3D coords (input) → LFQ tokens (target) | LFQ structure-tokenizer pretraining (the part that actually consumes 3D coords) |
| **CFP-Gen general** | Swiss-Prot (UniProtKB) + InterPro; backbone coords from PDB + AFDB | **103,939** (375 GO, 1,154 IPR) | **Sequence + multi-hot GO list + multi-hot IPR list + IPR-derived motif span + (optional IF path) backbone N/CA/C/O coords** | CFP-Gen stage-1/stage-2 function-conditioned generation (AGFM + RCFE) |
| **CFP-Gen enzyme** | SwissProt ∩ CARE; backbone coords from PDB + AFDB | **139,551** (661 EC, 4-level) | **Sequence + multi-hot GO/IPR lists + multi-hot EC list + motif span + (optional IF path) backbone coords** | CFP-Gen multi-catalytic enzyme design (EC-conditioned) |

## 5. Annotation-data detail (for the slide)

- **Frequency filter for CFP-Gen:** **≥100 sequences per GO term and per IPR domain** — applied to mitigate long-tail categories, following ProteoGAN's recommendation (`cfpgen_paper.md:859-862`). Resulting distribution: 30.6% of GO categories have 100–200 sequences, only 6.4% have &gt;1000; for IPR, 35.4% have 100–200, only 2.0% have &gt;1000 (`cfpgen_paper.md:874-878`).
- **CFP-Gen label encoding:** **multi-hot integer-ID lists padded with -1** to the longest list in each batch (not one-hot vectors at the data layer; one-hot happens inside the model's AGFM embedding lookup). Verified at `uniprotKB.py:283-289, 300-306`. Same scheme for GO, IPR, and EC. Note that the AGFM embeds each integer ID as a dense vector and sums across annotation types (`cfpgen_paper.md:298-311`).
- **DPLM-2 / DPLM have NO function annotations in training.** Confirmed by inspection: `TokenizedProteinDataset.__getitem__` returns only `struct_tokens`, `aatype_tokens`, `length`, `pdb_name` (`tokenized_protein.py:282-320`); `UniRefDataset.__getitem__` returns only the consensus string (`uniref.py:217-230`). Neither the on-disk CSV fields (`aa_seq`, `struct_seq`, `plddt`, `avg_plddt`, `cluster`, `split`, `pdb_name`) nor any collator output contains GO / IPR / EC / motif fields. Function is entirely absent from the DPLM / DPLM-2 data pipeline — this is the gap CFP-Gen addresses by attaching SwissProt/InterPro/CARE annotations on top of a DPLM-derived backbone.</result>

# Findings: Tokenizer Implementations in DPLM-2 and CFP-Gen

## 1. DPLM-2 LFQ Structure Tokenizer — Full Pipeline

### 1.1 Encoder: frozen ESM-IF1 GVP-Transformer
- **Class**: `GVPTransformerEncoderWrapper2` — `/home/cherry/dev/phd/dplm/src/byprot/models/structok/modules/gvp_encoder.py:53-83`.
- Loads the pretrained inverse-folding model `esm.pretrained.esm_if1_gvp4_t16_142M_UR50()` (line 56) and keeps only its `.encoder` (the GVP geometric encoder + Transformer, line 59).
- **Frozen by default** (`freeze=True`, line 54/61): every encoder parameter has `requires_grad_(False)` (lines 62-65), and the forward pass runs under `torch.set_grad_enabled(not self.freeze)` (line 79). Output dimension = `self.encoder.embed_tokens.embedding_dim` (line 66).
- **Input** = backbone atom coordinates (`backb_positions`, sliced to `[:, :, :3, :]` = N, CA, C at line 72); masked positions filled with `NaN` (line 75). The `VQModel.encode` calls it and then `.detach()`es the output (`structok_lfq.py:151`).
- Paper: "The encoder is based on a pre-trained GVP-Transformer [hsu2022esmif], with its parameters frozen during training" — `dplm2_paper.md:856-860` (appendix "Model Architecture"); also §3.3 at `dplm2_paper.md:383-385`.

### 1.2 pre_quant MLP → codebook_embed_dim = 13
- `structok_lfq.py:65-70`:
  ```
  pre_quant = nn.Sequential(
      nn.LayerNorm(encoder.embed_dim),
      nn.Linear(encoder.embed_dim, codebook_embed_dim),
      nn.ReLU(),
      nn.Linear(codebook_embed_dim, codebook_embed_dim),
  )
  ```
- `codebook_embed_dim` is driven by `codebook_config.embed_dim = 13` (config `structok_lfq_8k_pdb_swissprot_c512.yaml:55`). Masked positions are zeroed before quantization so they collapse to index 0 (`structok_lfq.py:158`).

### 1.3 LFQ quantizer (lookup-free)
- **Class**: `LFQ` — `/home/cherry/dev/phd/dplm/src/byprot/models/structok/modules/lfq.py:133`. Instantiated at `structok_lfq.py:58-63` with `dim=13`, `codebook_size=8192` (= 2^13, config line 54), `entropy_loss_weight=0.1`, `commitment_loss_weight=0.25` (config lines 56-57).
- **Binarization** (`lfq.py:293-296`): each of the 13 dims is sign-quantized to {-1, +1}: `quantized = torch.where(x &gt; 0, 1.0, -1.0)`.
- **Bit-to-index** (`lfq.py:183-185` and `:313-317`): the mask buffer is `2 ** torch.arange(codebook_dim-1, -1, -1)` = [2^12, …, 2^1, 2^0]; `indices = sum((quantized&gt;0).int() * mask)`. Equivalently `bits_to_indices` (`lfq.py:241-255`) computes `(bits * 2^arange(0,13)).sum(-1)`.
- This matches the paper equation `z_i = Σ_{k=1}^{log2|Z|} 2^{k-1} · 1{e_i[k] &gt; 0}` — `dplm2_paper.md:399` (§3.3).
- **Implicit codebook = 2^13 = 8192 entries** (`lfq.py:157` `codebook_size = 2**dim`; the actual `codebook` buffer at `:195-199` is materialized as `bits*2-1` only for entropy-logit computation, never looked up). The latent decomposition `C = ×_{k=1}^{log2|Z|} C_k, C_k={-1,1}` is stated at `dplm2_paper.md:389-393`.
- **Straight-through estimator**: `quantized = x + (quantized - x).detach()` (`lfq.py:363`).

### 1.4 post_quant + ESMFold decoder
- `structok_lfq.py:75-87`: `post_quant` is a `ModuleDict` with an MLP (LayerNorm→Linear→ReLU→Linear to `decoder.input_dim=128`) and a small `TransformerEncoder(input_dim, 8 heads, 4 layers)`.
- Decoder = `ESMFoldStructureDecoder` (`structok_lfq.py:22`, from `modules/folding_utils/decoder.py`): IPA-based AlphaFold2 structure module, 4 EvoFormer layers, no MSA row attention, following ESMFold. Config at `structok_lfq_8k_pdb_swissprot_c512.yaml:61-72` (`num_blocks: 4`, `sequence_state_dim: 128`, `pairwise_state_dim: 32`, `no_blocks: 8`, `no_angles: 7`). Reconstructs atom37 positions — `structok_lfq.py:245-255`.

### 1.5 Training losses (StructureVQLoss)
- **Class**: `StructureVQLoss` — `/home/cherry/dev/phd/dplm/src/byprot/models/structok/modules/loss.py:1702-1768`. It wraps `AlphaFoldLoss` (the reconstruction term) and adds the LFQ codebook loss.
- **Total** (line 1743): `loss = rec_loss + scaling_factor * codebook_weight(=1.0) * codebook_loss`.
- **Reconstruction (`AlphaFoldLoss.forward`, line 1777+)** assembles (loss.py:1812-1862):
  - `distogram` (line 612+, config weight in rec_loss)
  - `fape` — Frame Aligned Point Error (line 185, the primary reconstruction loss)
  - `lm_loss` — sequence-LM head cross-entropy against native sequence (line 786)
  - `violation` — between/within-residue structural violation loss (line 820+, weight 0.3 per config `structok_lfq_8k_pdb_swissprot_c512.yaml:84-85`)
  - `tm` — optional TM-score loss, gated by `config.tm.enabled` (line 1855-1858)
- **Codebook loss** (the LFQ auxiliary, from `lfq.py:385-388`): `commitment_loss_weight(0.25) * MSE_commit + entropy_loss_weight(0.1) * entropy_aux`. The entropy loss (`lfq.py:95-130`) minimizes per-sample entropy while maximizing batch/codebook entropy to encourage full codebook utilization.
- Paper: "reconstruction loss, codebook commitment loss, and entropy regularization loss … FAPE loss is used as the primary reconstruction loss … violation loss, and distogram loss from AlphaFold2 … sequence prediction head … cross-entropy against the native sequence" — `dplm2_paper.md:870-879`; also `dplm2_paper.md:400-404`.

### 1.6 Training data &amp; standalone-then-frozen protocol
- **Task**: `StrucTok` — `/home/cherry/dev/phd/dplm/src/byprot/tasks/struct_tokenizer/structok.py:40`. `step()` (line 142) runs the full encode→quantize→decode and calls `StructureVQLoss`; it is a self-contained Lightning task training only the tokenizer.
- **Data**: config `structok_lfq_8k_pdb_swissprot_c512.yaml:18-41` — `train_split: [pdb, afdb_swissprot]`, `crop_size: 512` (line 22), `eval_max_len: 512`. Paper: "trained using the same structure data … totaling 200K proteins" — `dplm2_paper.md:849-852`; and "trained on the same structure dataset as mentioned before" — `dplm2_paper.md:400-401`.
- **Standalone training**: `max_steps: 200_000`, lr 5e-4, AdamW (config lines 89-126). The encoder is frozen (`encoder_config.freeze: true`, line 59); the quantizer/pre_quant are trainable during this stage (`codebook_config.freeze: false`, line 53).
- **Frozen at main-model time**: when consumed by DPLM-2, the tokenizer is loaded via `get_struct_tokenizer(...)` lazily into `self._struct_tokenizer` (`dplm2.py:152-158`) purely as an encode/decode utility (`tokenize`/`detokenize`, `structok_lfq.py:214-255`); its parameters are never added to the DPLM-2 optimizer. The `freeze` flag in `codebook_config` exists precisely to flip it to `True` after standalone training (`structok_lfq.py:71-73`).

## 2. DPLM-2 Main-Model Vocabulary &amp; Embedding Layers

### 2.1 Unified vocabulary 33 + 8192 + 4 = 8229
- **Config**: `TokenizerConfig` — `/home/cherry/dev/phd/dplm/src/byprot/models/dplm2/dplm2.py:30-34`:
  ```
  vocab_file: str = "airkingbd/dplm2_650m"
  # amino acid tokens (33) + struct tokens (8192) + 4 special struct tokens
  vocab_size: int = field(default=33 + 8192 + 4)
  ```
- The actual size is set from the loaded tokenizer file: `self.cfg.tokenizer.vocab_size = len(self.tokenizer)` (`dplm2.py:80`).
- **Token composition** (from `_prepare_special_token`, `dplm2.py:168-197`, looked up in `DPLM2Tokenizer.from_pretrained("airkingbd/dplm2_650m")`):
  - **33 = AA + AA-special**: the 20 standard + non-standard `X, B, U, Z, O` (lines 191-195) plus AA control tokens `&lt;cls_aa&gt;`, `&lt;eos_aa&gt;`, `&lt;mask_aa&gt;`, `&lt;unk_aa&gt;`, `&lt;pad&gt;` (lines 169-176).
  - **8192 = struct token IDs** (the LFQ codebook, indices 0..8191).
  - **4 = struct-special**: `&lt;cls_struct&gt;`, `&lt;eos_struct&gt;`, `&lt;mask_struct&gt;`, `&lt;unk_struct&gt;` (lines 172-175). Hence the "+4".

### 2.2 ONE shared nn.Embedding word_embeddings table
- The net is `EsmForDPLM2` (`/home/cherry/dev/phd/dplm/src/byprot/models/dplm2/modules/dplm2_modeling_esm.py:658-661`), which subclasses `EsmForMaskedLM` and builds `self.esm = ModifiedEsmModel(config)` (line 662). `ModifiedEsmModel.__init__` sets `self.embeddings = EsmEmbeddings(config)` (line 488) — the standard HuggingFace `EsmEmbeddings`, whose only token table is a single `nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, config.hidden_size)` `word_embeddings`, resized to 8229 via `_get_resized_embeddings` (lines 725-825).
- `dplm2.py:229-232` (`forward`) feeds `input_ids` straight into `self.net(...)`, which routes AA and struct IDs through this one shared table. AA embeddings are initialized from the pretrained DPLM; struct rows are newly initialized (mean/std of existing rows, lines 816-822).

### 2.3 No separate modality/type embedding — inferred from token-id range
- `get_modality_type` — `dplm2.py:220-227`:
  ```
  modality_type = ((input_ids &lt; 33) &amp; input_mask).int()   # &lt;33 =&gt; AA(1); &gt;=33 =&gt; struct(0)
  modality_type[~input_mask] = self.pad_type              # 2 = padding
  ```
- `type_ids` is **not** an embedding-table lookup. It is consumed only by the **rotary position embedding** (`ModifiedRotaryEmbedding`, `dplm2_modeling_esm.py:28-85`), which halves the effective sequence length when both modalities are present so AA and struct halves share the same rotary phase (lines 42-43, 71-80). There is no `nn.Embedding` for token "type".

### 2.4 DPLM-2 Bit variant — cleaner separation (no shared struct table)
- **Class**: `DPLM2Bit` — `/home/cherry/dev/phd/dplm/src/byprot/models/dplm2/dplm2_bit.py:37`; net = `EsmForDPLM2Bit` — `/home/cherry/dev/phd/dplm/src/byprot/models/dplm2/modules/dplm2_bit_modeling_esm.py:638`.
- Struct tokens are **NOT** looked up in the shared word_embeddings table. Instead (`dplm2_bit_modeling_esm.py:660-670`):
  - `struct_bos_emb`, `struct_eos_emb`, `struct_mask_emb` are dedicated `nn.Parameter(torch.randn(hidden_size))` vectors for the 3 struct special tokens.
  - `quant2emb = nn.Linear(codebook_embed_dim(=13), config.hidden_size)` projects the 13-dim **binary code** (recovered via `struct_tokenizer.quantize.get_codebook_entry(...)`, `dplm2_bit.py:123-126`) directly to hidden dim. The struct BOS/EOS/mask positions overwrite the projected embedding (`dplm2_bit.py:128-134`).
- AA tokens still use the shared ESM embeddings (`dplm2_bit.py:120-121`: `input_aatype_embeds = self.net.esm.embeddings(...)`).
- **Output head** (`dplm2_bit_modeling_esm.py:645-655, 702-703`): `lm_head` predicts AA over the AA vocab; `lm_head_struct` is a **separate** `EsmLMHead` with `vocab_size = codebook_embed_dim * 2 = 26`, i.e. **binary classification per codebook dimension** (13 independent {-, +} decisions). Training target is `(get_codebook_entry(target - offset) &gt; 0).long()` (`dplm2_bit.py:188-193`); at inference, bits are sampled and summed with the LFQ mask to recover a token id (`dplm2_bit.py:328-336`).
- **Why cleaner**: the 8192-entry struct vocabulary never materializes as embedding/head rows — both input embedding and output prediction operate in the native 13-bit factorized space, decoupling model size from codebook size and matching the LFQ's factorized structure.

## 3. CFP-Gen's Function "Tokenizer" — What It Actually Is

### 3.1 No learned quantizer — just label-embedding tables
- **Class**: `FuncTagEmbedder` — `/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/src/byprot/models/lm/esm_cfpgen.py:210-220`:
  ```
  class FuncTagEmbedder(nn.Module):
      def __init__(self, num_classes, hidden_size):
          super().__init__()
          use_cfg_embedding = True
          self.embedding_table = nn.Embedding(num_classes + 1, hidden_size)
          self.num_classes = num_classes
      def forward(self, labels):
          return self.embedding_table(labels)
  ```
  The `+1` slot (`use_cfg_embedding`) is the classifier-free-guidance null token (index = `num_classes`), used when annotations are dropped.
- Three instances, one per annotation type (`CFPGenEncoder.__init__`, `esm_cfpgen.py:236-251`): `go_embedder`, `ipr_embedder`, `ec_embedder`, each `FuncTagEmbedder(config.{go,ipr,ec}_num, config.hidden_size)`.
- **Aggregation = summation across types** (`CFPGenEncoder.forward`, `esm_cfpgen.py:314-336`): GO/IPR/EC embeddings are produced by `drop_anno_ids` (which sums across the multiple label IDs within one type, `esm_cfpgen.py:288-307`, via `torch.sum(torch.stack(class_embeds), dim=0)`), then the three per-type vectors are **added**: `anno_embed = anno_embed + ipr_embed` then `+ ec_embed`.
- **Entry into the model = FiLM**, not as an input token. `anno_embed` is passed as `cond_input` to every `AGFMLayer` (`esm_cfpgen.py:407-454`), where `adaLN_modulation` (SiLU→Linear→6*hidden) produces `(shift_msa, scale_msa, gate_msa, shift_mlp, scale_mlp, gate_mlp)` that `modulate` the LayerNorm'd features (`esm_cfpgen.py:84-113, 199-209`). This is the Annotation-Guided Feature Modulation (AGFM).

### 3.2 Vocabulary = the ontology label sets themselves
- Configs (`/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/configs/experiment/cfpgen/`):
  - General model: `go_num: 375`, `ipr_num: 1154`, `ec_num: 661` — `cfpgen-if_650m_stage2.yaml:37,40,43` and `cfpgen_650m_stage1.yaml:30,33,36`.
  - Enzyme model: `go_num: 780`, `ipr_num: 4982`, `ec_num: 661` — `cfpgen_enzyme_650m.yaml:30,33,36`.
- These IDs are **raw ontology integer IDs** (GO terms, InterPro domains, EC numbers), not learned codes — there is no encoder, no codebook, no quantization. The "codebook" is fixed by the external ontology and its size is just the label-set cardinality.
- Paper: "annotation tags (e.g., GO terms, IPR domains and EC numbers) are encoded as one-hot embeddings and injected to the model through an Annotation-Guided Feature Modulation (AGFM) module" — `cfpgen_paper.md:52-55`. (Note: the paper text says "one-hot embeddings" but the code is a dense `nn.Embedding` lookup — functionally an learned embedding table, not literal one-hot.)

### 3.3 CFP-Gen's structure branch uses DPLM-1's GVP-Transformer, NOT DPLM-2's LFQ tokenizer
- Structure conditioning $f_{\text{GVPT}}$ is a **GVP-Transformer** (`cfpgen_paper.md:225-228`: "GVPT indicates the GVP-Transformer [hsu2022learning] for encoding 3D [structures]"), wired in via a **cross-attention adapter** — not as discrete struct tokens.
- The IF variant implements this as `AGFMAdapter` with `self.adapter_crossattention = ModifiedEsmAttention(config, kdim, vdim)` (`/home/cherry/dev/phd/cfpgen/src/byprot/models/lm/esm_cfpgen_if.py:341-353, 432`), consuming `encoder_hidden_states` (the GVP features). This is the DPLM-1 structure-conditioning recipe (pretrained GVP encoder + cross-attention adapter), not DPLM-2's LFQ discrete vocabulary.

### 3.4 Contrast
- **DPLM-2 (structure)**: continuous 3D coords → *learned* LFQ quantizer → 8192-entry *learned* codebook → discrete struct *tokens* consumed as first-class sequence positions.
- **CFP-Gen (function)**: external ontology IDs → plain per-type `nn.Embedding` lookups → summed → FiLM condition. No compression, no learned codebook, no generative modeling of the function vocabulary itself.

---

## 4. Slide-Ready Contrast Table

| Dimension | DPLM-2 LFQ structure tokenizer | CFP-Gen function "tokenizer" (FuncTagEmbedder / AGFM) |
|---|---|---|
| **What is being tokenized** | 3D backbone coordinates (continuous) | Function annotations GO / IPR / EC (discrete ontology IDs) |
| **Vocabulary source** | LEARNED codebook — 2^13 = 8192 implicit LFQ entries (`lfq.py:157`; paper §3.3) | External ontology label sets themselves — GO=375/780, IPR=1154/4982, EC=661 (configs; `esm_cfpgen.py:236-251`) |
| **Quantization** | Sign binarization of 13 latent dims to {-1,+1}; index = Σ 2^(k-1)·bit (`lfq.py:293-296, 313-317`; paper eq. `dplm2_paper.md:399`) | NONE — IDs used directly as embedding-table indices |
| **Embedding into main model** | ONE shared `nn.Embedding` word_embeddings for AA+struct (`dplm2_modeling_esm.py:488`; `dplm2.py:34`). Bit variant: `quant2emb` Linear + `lm_head_struct` binary head (`dplm2_bit_modeling_esm.py:660-670`) | Three SEPARATE `nn.Embedding` tables (one per GO/IPR/EC), summed, then FiLM (`esm_cfpgen.py:210-220, 314-336, 199-209`) |
| **Modality signal** | Inferred from token-id range (&lt;33 = AA, ≥33 = struct) via `get_modality_type` (`dplm2.py:220-227`); no type embedding | Implicit — which embedder table the ID indexes into |
| **Trained standalone** | YES — own task `StrucTok`, own loss `StructureVQLoss`, 200K PDB+SwissProt, crop 512, 200K steps (`structok.py:40`; `structok_lfq_8k...yaml`; paper `dplm2_paper.md:849-852`) | N/A — no separate pretraining; embedding tables train jointly with the main model |
| **Auxiliary losses** | FAPE + distogram + seq-LM + violation + TM + entropy(0.1) + commitment(0.25) (`loss.py:1702-1768, 1812-1862`; `lfq.py:385-388`) | None (only the downstream diffusion/MASKed-LM loss flows through the FiLM path) |
| **How it enters the main model** | As first-class INPUT TOKENS in the unified sequence (struct tokens sit alongside AA tokens; `dplm2.py:229-232`) | As a FiLM CONDITION (shift/scale/gate) modulating every AGFM layer (`esm_cfpgen.py:199-209, 407-454`) — never a token |
| **Frozen after pretraining** | YES — encoder frozen throughout; quantizer/pre_quant frozen at main-model time (`gvp_encoder.py:62-65`; `structok_lfq.py:71-73`) | N/A (trains end-to-end) |
| **Generative over the codebook** | YES — DPLM-2 diffusion samples struct token IDs (or 13 bits in the Bit variant) (`dplm2_bit.py:254-336`; `dplm2.py`) | NO — function IDs are conditions, never generated |
